places.name: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park (Uluru/Ayers Rock)
places.ai_summary: Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage site, home to the iconic Uluru and the domed Kata Tjuta formations. It offers cultural insights and stunning natural landscapes.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary seasonally.

places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to learn about the cultural significance of Uluru.
places.address: Uluru Rd, Petermann NT 0872, Australia

places.name: Kakadu National Park
places.ai_summary: Kakadu National Park is a biodiverse nature reserve in Australia's Northern Territory. It features wetlands, rivers, and ancient rock art sites.

opening_hours.notes: Closed during extreme weather conditions.

places.place_tip: Explore the rock art galleries at Ubirr and Nourlangie.
places.address: Kakadu Hwy, Jabiru NT 0886, Australia

places.name: Kata Tjuta (The Olgas)
places.ai_summary: Kata Tjuta, also known as The Olgas, is a group of large, domed rock formations located in the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park. They are sacred to the Indigenous Anangu people and offer stunning views, especially at sunrise and sunset.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary seasonally.

places.place_tip: Walk the Valley of the Winds trail for a close-up experience of the domes.
places.address: Kata Tjuta Rd, Petermann NT 0872, Australia

places.name: Kings Canyon (Watarrka National Park)
places.ai_summary: Kings Canyon, located in Watarrka National Park, is known for its stunning sandstone gorge, towering cliffs, and diverse plant and animal life. The Rim Walk offers breathtaking views.

places.place_tip: The Rim Walk is challenging but offers the best views. Carry enough water.
places.address: Kings Canyon Rd, Watarrka NT 0872, Australia

places.name: Litchfield National Park
places.ai_summary: Litchfield National Park is known for its waterfalls, swimming holes, and magnetic termite mounds. It's a popular destination for both tourists and locals seeking a natural retreat.

opening_hours.notes: Some areas may be closed during the wet season.

places.place_tip: Visit the waterfalls early in the morning to avoid crowds.
places.address: Litchfield Park Rd, Batchelor NT 0845, Australia

places.name: Nitmiluk National Park (Katherine Gorge)
places.ai_summary: Nitmiluk National Park, also known as Katherine Gorge National Park, features stunning gorges, waterfalls, and rich Aboriginal culture. The park is famous for its boat tours and hiking trails.

opening_hours.notes: Boat tours operate seasonally.

places.place_tip: Take a boat tour to see the gorges from the water.
places.address: Nitmiluk Rd, Nitmiluk NT 0852, Australia

places.name: Darwin Waterfront Precinct
places.ai_summary: The Darwin Waterfront Precinct is a vibrant area featuring a wave lagoon, sandy beach, and a variety of restaurants and shops. It's a popular spot for both relaxation and entertainment.

opening_hours.notes: Some facilities may have extended hours.

places.place_tip: Enjoy the sunset by the wave lagoon.
places.address: Darwin City NT 0800, Australia

opening_hours.notes: Last entry at 16:30.

places.place_tip: Attend the free-flying bird show and visit the nocturnal house.

places.name: Royal Flying Doctor Service Tourist Facility
places.ai_summary: The Royal Flying Doctor Service Tourist Facility in Alice Springs offers an insight into the world-renowned medical service. The facility features interactive exhibits and a short film about the service's history and operations.
places.name_english: Royal Flying Doctor Service Tourist Facility

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Christmas Day and Good Friday.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the Alice Springs Telegraph Station.

places.name: Simpsons Gap
places.ai_summary: Simpsons Gap is a prominent gap in the West MacDonnell Ranges, known for its towering cliffs and resident black-footed rock wallabies. It's a great spot for a short walk and wildlife viewing.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary seasonally.

places.place_tip: Look for rock wallabies among the rocks.

places.name: Tiwi Islands
places.ai_summary: The Tiwi Islands, north of Darwin, are known for their Indigenous culture, art, and beautiful beaches. The islands offer a unique insight into the Aboriginal way of life.

opening_hours.notes: Access by ferry or plane. Check seasonal availability.

attribution.title: Folklore and Science Meet at Tiwi
attribution.author: NASA Earth Observatory images by Joshua Stevens, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey. Story by Kasha Patel.
attribution.description:
According to ancient folklore, the creation of the main Tiwi Islands—Bathurst and Melville—can be traced to an old blind woman named Mudungkala. As the world was taking form during the Palaneri (or “dreaming” phase), Mudungkala rose from the Earth in the southeast of Melville Island. Crawling on her knees, she carried her three infants and slowly traveled north.

As she made her journey, fresh water bubbled up in her wake, creating tides and the Clarence and Dundas Straits that separate the islands from mainland Australia today. As she continued around the landmass, she decided it was too large and formed the Apsley Strait to divide the island into two. She then covered the bare islands with vegetation and animals so her children could have food once she left. Once the islands were complete, she vanished, leaving no clues about where she went.

The images on this page show various scenes of the Tiwi Islands, which are part of Australia’s Northern Territory and located about 60 kilometers (40 miles) north of Darwin. Both images were acquired on August 10, 2019, by the Operational Land Imager on the Landsat 8 satellite.

The Tiwi folklore may not be far off from how the islands developed. Researchers interpret the narrative as a story of the landmass settling and then experiencing subsequent flooding—an ancient account of sea level rise. The Tiwi Islands were once connected to continental Australia, but rapid sea level rise separated the islands from the mainland and each other. Researchers have calculated that the flooding around the Tiwi Islands occurred between 8,200 and 9,650 years ago.

Because the islands were isolated from mainland Australia, the Tiwi people developed a distinct culture over thousands of years. Tiwi (which means “one people”) speak one language, although there may be three to four different variations of the language. About 90 percent of the 3,000 island inhabitants are Aborigines. The most populous town is Milikapti, home to around 450 people.

Climate change might bring more sea level changes in the future. Climate projections predict a further increase in air temperature, tropical cyclones, storm surge height, and sea surface temperature around this part of Australia. And researchers have predicted that the region could experience sea level rise up to 1.1 meters (3.6 feet) by 2100.

places.name: Arnhem Land
places.ai_summary: Arnhem Land is a remote and rugged area in the Northern Territory, known for its Indigenous culture, rock art, and natural beauty. Access is limited, and permits are required.

opening_hours.notes: Access by permit only. Check with the Northern Land Council.

places.place_tip: Respect the local customs and guidelines.
places.address: Arnhem Land NT, Australia

places.name: Finke Gorge National Park
places.ai_summary: Finke Gorge National Park is known for its stunning landscapes, including the ancient Finke River, palm valleys, and rugged mountains. It's a great destination for hiking and exploring Aboriginal culture.

opening_hours.notes: Some areas may be closed during the wet season.

places.place_tip: Visit the Palm Valley and take the Finke River cruise.
places.address: Finke Gorge National Park NT, Australia

places.name: Karlu Karlu / Devils Marbles Conservation Reserve
places.ai_summary: Karlu Karlu, also known as the Devils Marbles, is a conservation reserve famous for its large, round boulders scattered across the landscape. The site is sacred to the Aboriginal people and offers a unique geological phenomenon.
places.name_english: Karlu Karlu / Devils Marbles Conservation Reserve

opening_hours.notes: Camping is allowed in designated areas.

places.place_tip: Visit at sunrise or sunset for stunning photographic opportunities.
places.address: Karlu Karlu Rd, Wauchope NT 0872, Australia

places.name: Field of Light Uluru (Tili Wiru Tjuta Nyakutjaku)
places.ai_summary: The Field of Light is a solar-powered art installation by Bruce Munro, located near Uluru. It features over 50,000 spindles of light that illuminate the desert landscape at night.
places.name_english: Field of Light Uluru (Tili Wiru Tjuta Nyakutjaku)

opening_hours.notes: Closed during the day. Advance booking recommended.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the sunset at Uluru.
places.address: Uluru Rd, Petermann NT 0872, Australia

places.name: Ormiston Gorge
places.ai_summary: Ormiston Gorge is a picturesque gorge in the West MacDonnell Ranges, known for its waterhole, walking trails, and stunning scenery. It's a great spot for swimming and picnicking.

opening_hours.notes: Hours may vary seasonally.

places.place_tip: Take the Ormiston Pound Walk for stunning views.

places.name: West MacDonnell National Park

places.place_tip: Visit the Ochre Pits and Ormiston Gorge.
